fact_sheet.business_description: The basket comprises compute design (Nvidia), outsourced fabrication (TSMC), cloud infrastructure (Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet), and incumbent consumer/software platforms (Meta). These entities form a thematic ecosystem where large language models require compute, cloud providers supply access, and platforms distribute AI features to users [D01].

Incumbent platforms cannibalizing products with expensive inference [D05]

gate1.edge_statement: The event is the secular AI compute inflection; the mispricing is the market's focus on short-term monetization risk over long-term infrastructure necessity, and our edge is our early thematic synthesis of the AI ecosystem.
gate1.one_line_verdict: a thematic basket of AI infrastructure leaders benefiting from an accelerating capex and compute cycle

gate2.variant_view: The market is fixated on short-term monetization concerns and the high cost of inference, leading to a skepticism that AI capex will drive sustainable earnings growth [D05]. We believe this ignores the fundamental necessity of this infrastructure for the next cycle of compute, where the inflection in demand is already visible in hyperscaler capex and production capacity [D01], [D03]. We expect the market to re-rate these companies as the underlying AI compute cycle translates into accelerating cloud and platform growth [D03].

final.memo:
We are establishing a basket position in the AI infrastructure ecosystem, comprising compute design leaders, critical foundry capacity, and incumbent cloud platforms. The market has mispriced this opportunity by hyper-focusing on short-term inference costs and monetization uncertainty, while ignoring the visible secular inflection in hyperscaler capex and compute demand [D01], [D05].

Our sum-of-the-parts valuation relies on the underlying earnings power of these franchises, which possess significant defensive qualities. Companies like Alphabet and Microsoft hold massive net cash positions of $99.894bn and $56.217bn, respectively, providing a hard floor for our investment [D04]. We benchmark these assets against historical tech sector P/E multiples, anticipating a re-rating as revenue growth validates current capital intensity [D06].

We observe a clear demand signal, evidenced by Azure's 26-27% growth rate and Meta's aggressive $30-33bn capex plan for 2023 [D03]. This is not a speculative turnaround but a thematic investment in the essential infrastructure of the next compute cycle. We expect this inflection to drive 25-30% IRR over our three-year holding period [D03].

Our role is that of a thematic investor rather than an activist; this opportunity requires no governance intervention, as corporate actors are already responding to the secular mandate for AI deployment [D03]. We will monitor hyperscaler capex and fabrication capacity for signs of exhaustion, exiting immediately if the monetization thesis breaks [D03], [D05].

We are sizing this at 5% of NAV to reflect our conviction in the thematic transition, while mitigating broader market beta via index put options [D08]. We remain vigilant regarding the risk of a multi-year capex glut, which remains our primary kill criterion for the position [D05].
